title: Examining form-based linguistic productivity in people and large language models
abstract: arXiv:2610.33433v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Linguistic productivity, as evidenced by the use of words in novel contexts, is one of the most striking facts about human language. However, how abstract the knowledge that enables such productivity is remains unclear. We compare people's and computational language models' linguistic productivity in contexts where successful generalization depends on form-based information. We focus on extending the use of a novel verb learned in the active voice to passive contexts. We find people extend active to passive uses in a way consistent with abstract generalizations concerning linguistic form, even when no plausible meaning can be assigned to the novel verb. In contrast, large language models succeeded only when a meaning like an existing verb's could be assigned to the novel verb. translated_title: 检验人类与大型语言模型中基于形式的语言能产性
translated_abstract: 语言能产性，即词语在新语境中的使用，是人类语言最显著的特征之一。然而，支撑这种能产性的知识究竟有多抽象仍不清楚。我们在成功泛化依赖于基于形式的信息的情境中，比较了人类与计算语言模型的语言能产性。我们专注于将主动语态中学到的新动词的使用扩展到被动语态语境中。我们发现，即使无法为新动词赋予合理的意义，人们仍能以一种与关于语言形式的抽象泛化相一致的方式，将主动用法扩展到被动用法。相比之下，大型语言模型只有在新动词能够被赋予类似现有动词的意义时才能成功。我们得出结论：计算模型的句法知识仍然与特定词汇项的分布和意义紧密绑定，而人类的句法知识则不然。
tldr: 该研究发现人类能够基于抽象的语言形式规则将新动词从主动语态泛化到被动语态，而大型语言模型只有在新动词具有类似已知动词的意义时才能成功，表明计算模型的句法知识仍依赖于具体词汇的分布与意义，缺乏人类那样的抽象性。
en_tdlr: Humans generalize novel verbs from active to passive voice based on abstract linguistic form even without plausible meanings, whereas large language models succeed only when a meaningful interpretation is available, revealing that computational models' syntactic knowledge remains tied to specific lexical items rather than being abstract like human syntactic knowledge.
